description: Every dependency is pinned so a build is reproducible; Renovate is what moves the pins, as PRs a human approves.

pip_requirements.description: pip-compile owns the yamllint lock; this manager would match the same file.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Any Monday run; the preset's Monday 00:00-03:59 UTC window never contains the workflow's daily 04:17 UTC start.

packageRules.description: go.mod's go line is the project's only Go version, so it follows every Go release; Renovate leaves it alone by default.
Indirect modules are pinned in go.mod like any other, so they move with every release too; Renovate leaves them alone by default.
The renovate-version input of renovatebot/github-action has no place to write a digest, so a digest pin of it can never be applied.
The supported Kea is the latest stable 3.x release: ISC's odd minors are development releases, and the -alpine tags are a different image.
The compatibility check on a Kea update tests the new Kea against current main, so the pull request follows main.
README names the tested Kea by version alone, so there is no digest there to pin.

customManagers.description: Tools CI runs as `go run <module>/cmd/<tool>@vX.Y.Z`; the dependency is the module, not the package.
The Kea the compatibility check runs against, and the version README names as tested: one dependency in two places, so they move in one pull request.
